 French Open: Toma Unblocks View
 Wednesday, October 21, 2026
 TEXT BY DIANNE PIERRE | LUCAS NOYON/BADMINTONPHOTO 
 SHARE 
 Toma Junior Popov delivered the standout result of the YONEX French Open 2026 opening round, stunning top seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn 9-21 21-14 21-15 in their fifth career meeting.
 When the draw was released, Popov’s immediate reaction was “again”. It’s their third meeting this year.
 “I thought, ‘Fine, no problem. I will go for it’. I had the home crowd. It wasn’t an easy draw but I had nothing to lose so I just had to enjoy it.’”
 The Frenchman arrived in Paris extra motivated after an underwhelming performance at last week’s Denmark Open.
 “I wanted my revenge. Last week, it was a bit of a below-par performance so I wanted to come back and show my level, especially at home.”
 Vitidsarn took control early, capitalising on both the conditions and Toma’s errors to claim the opening game.
 “I had a bit of bad luck. My side was a slower, so when he pushed the shuttles, they slowed down at the back of the court. He pushed me a lot and I couldn’t make the most of it. I also made a lot of easy mistakes, giving him opportunities, which opened up the court for him.”
 Backed by a vocal crowd, Toma found a way back into the contest and never looked back.
 “He pushed me a lot and brought me back into the game. I looked at him thinking, ‘Good, you are helping me’.”
 The victory marked the first time Toma had beaten the world No.1 since 2021 but he kept the achievement in perspective.
 “It gives me a lot of confidence but it’s only one win. I will have to prove myself in the next round and keep doing so. Good to win against the world No.1.”
 Vitidsarn was gracious in defeat, praising Toma’s all-round game while admitting fatigue took its toll as the match wore on.
 “He can play any style,” said the Asian Games champion. “I’m very tired, my performance wasn’t good enough to win today.”
 Toma’s day got better – later in the evening he combined with younger brother Christo to defeat fifth seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy/Chirag Shetty 21-19 18-21 21-13.

 WHAT OTHERS SAID 
 “I don’t know how many times we’ve gone right to the end. Maybe once but it was really exciting.” – Mads Vestegaard after he and Daniel Lundgaard went the distance against Lee Jhe-Huei/Yang Po-Hsuan 21-18 30-29 to reach the second round
 “She’s getting stronger. Her footwork is very strong, I can see she’s been working on that by the way she moves on court but maybe I got lucky today.” – Pornpawee Chochuwong compliments Karunpathevan Letshanna after winning 23-21 21-15
 “We both had a tough draw last week in Denmark and we promised each other this would be our week.” – Mia Blichfeldt after cheering for boyfriend Toma following her own win over good friend Kirsty Gilmour
 Good day in Paris for the love birds.
